notes:
Summary: mid-market SaaS (product: customer support automation). Evaluating hosted API first (pilot) then committed Dedicated. Primary constraint = strict EU data residency for user transcripts and derived embeddings. Key quote from CTO: "We cannot have user data leave the EU for legal/regulatory reasons". Current status: hosted API pilot ok for feature validation but fails residency requirement; evaluating Dedicated in eu-west-1 + replication design.

POC details / technical asks:
- Workloads: chat assistants (session-focused), embeddings for semantic search, occasional reranking for prioritization rules.
- Targets: chat p95 < 120ms for response generation (short prompts, 1024 context), embeddings 200 QPS steady with 800 QPS hourly peaks, 99.9% availability for inference endpoints.
- Model preferences: open models with quantized variants; prefer ability to pin model versions and have fallback to smaller quantized variant when under heavy load.
- Routing: want primary EU routing (eu-west-1) with optional NA fallback only for anonymized metadata; legal prefers no cross-border token-level data movement.
- Caching/Batching: team interested in KV prefix caching and batching recommendations from Redwood Optimize to meet cost targets.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget; target ARR 50–150k; would accept a committed monthly/annual Dedicated plan with burst credits.

Security / compliance notes:
- Required: SSO (SAML), audit logs, KMS integration, DPA with explicit EU residency clause, retention controls for transcripts (default 90 days, option to reduce).
- Security team asked for architecture diagram showing flow for cache/replica failover without exporting raw tokens out of EU.

POC plan and next steps:
- Redwood to provide dedicated capacity proposal and two pricing options: (A) 6-month commit + burst, (B) 12-month commit with lower unit price. Include estimated token/unit economics for embeddings vs chat.
- Schedule POC run in eu-west-1 week of 2026-04-06 (2-week window) to validate: p95 latency, throughput, and fallback behavior when capacity is exhausted.
- Legal: iterate DPA + addendum for data residency; expected sign-off timeline 3-4 weeks after POC if metrics meet SLA.

Open questions / Blockers (short):
- Legal wants explicit guarantee that identifiable data never leaves EU (needs mapping to Redwood routing/fallback policy).
- Need clarity on multi-region read replicas for embeddings search without replicating raw vectors outside EU.
- SE asks: can Redwood support dedicated nodes physically in FRA region (eu-central-1) vs. eu-west-1 for lower network hop for customers in DE?

Action items assigned:

- Riley (AE): deliver dedicated pricing deck + legal contact intro; chase DPA redlines.
- Leo (CSM): prep onboarding checklist and two-week runbook for the POC environment.
